A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoVE-KD study, with readable methods, equations, experiments, and figures supporting comparison. Both supplied files end with references; neither includes the appendix mentioned in Section 4.1.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, and attention visualizations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluations of the SAM-L-augmented MoVE-KD-v1.1 configuration.

M1.justification: v2 introduces MoVE-KD-v1.1 with SAM-L added to the original CLIP, EVA-02, and ConvNeXt teachers. This is a limited teacher-ensemble extension; encoder adapters, MoLE routing, attention weighting, and the losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LLaVA training datasets and eight evaluation benchmarks. Adding SAM-L as a pretrained teacher does not introduce a segmentation evaluation or another dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same LLaVA, LLaVA-NeXT, InstructBLIP, Qwen-VL, and RADIO comparisons. The original MoVE-KD results are renamed v1.0, while the added rows evaluate the proposed v1.1 variant.

E3.justification: The new experiment compares three-teacher and four-teacher configurations for the existing LLaVA-1.5 1.7B, 7B, and 13B models. Previously reported training procedures, benchmarks, and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds an analysis of whether an additional SAM-L teacher improves performance across model sizes. Existing component, freezing, and CLIP-weight analyses remain. Figure 5 retains its four attention examples but removes the per-image teacher-weight examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The Avg columns remain benchmark aggregates rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds 24 scores for the four-teacher variant, with mixed effects: at 7B, TextVQA is 59.6 versus 58.3 with three teachers, while MME is 1509.1 versus 1524.5. Table 4 changes the 0.8-weight row's TextVQA from 58.4 to 58.3 and Avg from 58.5 to 68.0. Figure 1 corrects LLaVA's VQA value from 79.5 to 78.5, but its new v1.1 GQA label, 63.8, conflicts with Table 1's 63.9. Figure 5 removes numerical teacher weights.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, encoder-fusion, attention-guided distillation, and performance claims. The additional teacher experiment does not redefine the headline contributions.

C2.justification: The new Section 4.3 paragraph interprets the SAM-L experiment as evidence of strong scalability with more teachers, without discussing its per-metric regressions. Existing interpretations concerning forgetting, foreground/background attention, teacher weighting, and the possible projector bottleneck remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promise to release code into a statement of availability with a repository address. v2 also identifies SAM-L for the added configuration. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, and the 16-A800 hardware disclosure remain unchanged; repository availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kirillov et al.'s Segment Anything reference to support the SAM-L experiment. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against earlier distillation methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds the more-teachers paragraph and an acknowledgement, updates affiliations and variant names, and makes limited wording edits. The section sequence and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 adds variant rows and revised highlighting. Figure 1 adds the v1.1 curve and reduces eight axes to six by omitting MME and POPE. Figure 5 is reformatted without teacher-weight annotations, while the method diagrams retain their content with sizing and rendering changes.

improvement.justification: The additional teacher-count experiment, corrected Table 4 values, and explicit code-access pointer modestly improve empirical support and reproducibility documentation. These benefits are tempered by removal of the per-image teacher weights, a new Figure 1/Table 1 GQA discrepancy, and scalability wording that overlooks regressions visible in Table 1.
